implementation.name: original-v2-shadow-deployment
implementation.scope: The original shadow and canary panels. Declared toy batch R0–R19. Shadow copies every input; the separate canary batch sends one of twenty requests to the candidate, matching the illustrated 5 percent stage. No latency or quality result is assumed.
implementation.question: When can a candidate response reach a user?

purpose: When can a candidate response reach a user?
storyboard: The proxy receives R0–R19. Production remains the only authority for user responses.
The proxy sends each input to production and a copy to the isolated candidate. The same request identities appear in both execution paths.
Production outputs return to users. Candidate outputs are logged for comparison and cannot enter the response path.
Both outputs can be compared offline. The candidate has executed the same batch in addition to production, but no user has seen its answers.
Start a separate batch of R0–R19 for the canary comparison. Here the splitter chooses one model for each request; it does not mirror every input.
Requests R0–R18 go to production; R19 goes to the candidate. This is the declared one-of-twenty illustration of the original 5 percent stage.
Production answers its nineteen requests and the candidate answers R19. Candidate behavior is now exposed to one live user in this toy batch.
The illustrated stage stays at 5 percent until measured evidence supports a change. SLO or error drift requires rollback; shadow comparison alone cannot reveal user reactions to unseen outputs.
guard: Shadow candidate cannot answer users. The toy canary split illustrates the source 5 percent stage, not a deterministic batching requirement. Capacity cost is additional model execution, not a latency claim; rollout and rollback remain evidence-dependent.
